narrative.text: Introduces a 2021 infographic snapshot of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in Kuwait, explaining that it summarises national data across the life course to help set priorities and plan programmes. It notes the data come from international sources and that intersectionality and non-binary gender categories are poorly captured.

Presents demographic, sexual and reproductive health and HIV data for Kuwait, including a population of 4.3 million, life expectancy, a fertility rate of 2.1, a low adolescent birth rate and neonatal mortality of 4.5 per 1000 live births. Most HIV indicators are marked as having no data, and a context note links SRHR to the SDGs and universal health coverage.

Summarises Kuwait's laws and policies affecting SRHR, showing for example that HIV transmission is criminalized, entry for people with HIV is restricted, PrEP is available but self-testing is not allowed. It also records that abortion is allowed only to save a woman's life or for foetal impairment, spousal consent is required for married women's SRH services, and same-sex behaviour, sex work and drug offences carry punitive laws.

Presents health system indicators for Kuwait, including a UHC service coverage index of 76, legislation on universal health coverage, health workforce density and health spending of 5% of GDP. It notes no condom stock-outs and both paper and electronic health information systems, while several indicators lack data.

Presents reproductive health service indicators for Kuwait, where nearly all births are attended by skilled personnel but most contraception, antenatal care, HIV and syphilis testing and abortion indicators have no data. A note stresses women's right to choose whether and when to have children and to access quality reproductive care.

Presents sexual health service indicators for Kuwait, showing most HIV prevention and treatment cascade data are missing, 41 current PrEP users, and services for survivors of rape such as emergency contraception and post-exposure prophylaxis. It records no national HPV vaccination or cervical cancer screening programme.

Presents indicators on harmful practices, sexuality education, adolescent sexual health and key populations in Kuwait, with most fields lacking data apart from population size and HIV prevalence estimates for people who inject drugs and prisoners.

The first page of endnotes for the Kuwait SRHR snapshot, noting the April 2021 data cutoff and giving the year and source of each indicator, mainly UN population data, WHO and UNFPA publications and DHS surveys, with many marked as no data.

Continues the endnotes for the Kuwait SRHR snapshot, citing sources such as the World Economic Forum, UNAIDS laws and policies analytics, the WHO Global Health Observatory and expenditure database for indicators on gender, health systems and services.

The back page of the Kuwait SRHR snapshot, with a disclaimer, the WHO 2021 licence statement and the remaining endnotes on services for rape survivors, cervical cancer, child marriage, sexuality education and key populations, several noting no known source.
